newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan economy recovering despite stocks plunge-EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan economy recovering despite stocks plunge-EPA.

text.p: Japan's economy is continuing to recover gradually despite sharp falls in Tokyo share prices, the government's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said in its monthly economic report released on Tuesday.
"Although stock prices are falling, the current state of the economy is that it is continuing to recover gradually and is more or less firm," an EPA official told reporters.
The phraseology of the government's monthly economic assessment, which is closely watched by markets for signs of policy shifts, was unchanged from December.
"Our country's economy continues to recover, although the pace of the recovery is slow," the January report said.

On the Tokyo stock market, the Nikkei average of 225 leading shares fell more than 2,000 points last week on worries about the economy and the health of financial institutions, but on Monday it ended back above 18,000 on a technical rebound.
The official said falls in share prices may have some negative impact on business sentiment, but that the impact would be limited if the drop was only for a short period.
The impact of weaker business sentiment on corporate capital spending would also be confined, he said.
He said corporate capital spending was rising and firms would be forced to carry out their investment plans to survive various structural reforms in the economy.

The EPA official said he was aware some people were worried that stock price falls would slice banks' unrealised profits, undermine their ability to deal with risks, dampen their lending, slow down the pace of writing off problem loans and affect their international capital adequacy ratios.
But given weak fund demand in Japan, the banks' lending was unlikely to be greatly affected, he said.
If share price falls contributed to a drop in long-term interest rates, this might even have a positive effect on the economy, he added.

"The government will continue to promote various economic structural reforms, including deregulation and will work towards managing the economy properly to strengthen economic recovery and secure the continuation of stable growth in the medium to longer term," the report said.
Government optimism was underlined in the report by slight improvements in employment data and growth in exports.

Net exports, which had been on a declining trend, had been moving sideways on the back of slower growth in imports, especially of cars and semiconductors. Exports were also strong, supported by good sales of machine tools and automobiles, the EPA official said. "For now, there are no factors that could boost imports," he said.

The report said that although the unemployment rate was still near record-high levels, the number of unemployed in November fell from a year earlier for the first time since April 1992. The number of those forced to quit their jobs also showed year-on-year declines in November, it said.
The report said declines in domestic wholesale prices had stopped, although consumer prices remained stable.
The EPA official said this was due to rises in global oil and copper prices and weakness in the yen against the dollar, as well as tighter demand/supply conditions in Japan.
